content: If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, this medication should only be used when absolutely necessary. Its use during the first two months of pregnancy may slightly increase the risk of birth defects. Additionally, prolonged use or high doses near the expected delivery date may harm the unborn baby. To minimize risks, use the smallest effective dose for the shortest duration possible. This medication can pass into breast milk and may cause undesirable effects in a nursing infant. Notify your doctor immediately if your baby shows signs of unusual sleepiness, difficulty feeding, or trouble breathing. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. The risk of severe side effects, such as slow or shallow breathing, extreme drowsiness, or dizziness, may increase if this medication is taken with other products that cause drowsiness or breathing problems. Check the labels of all your medications, including allergy or cough-and-cold products, as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. In the event of an overdose, if the person has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Do not share this medication with others. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This medication is used to treat diarrhea by decreasing the frequency of bowel movements and slowing intestinal movement. Take it by mouth as directed by your doctor, usually four times daily. Do not use a household spoon, as it may not provide the correct dose. Do not inject this medication. If you suddenly stop using this medication, you may experience withdrawal symptoms such as sweating, nausea, vomiting, or restlessness. To prevent withdrawal, your doctor may gradually reduce your dose. Withdrawal is more likely if you have used this medication for a long time or in high doses. While this medication helps many people, it may sometimes cause addiction, especially if you have a history of substance use disorder. Do not increase your dose, take it more often, or use it for longer than prescribed. Diarrhea can sometimes lead to dehydration. It is important to drink adequate fluids and electrolytes to prevent this. Contact your doctor immediately if you develop signs of dehydration, such as decreased urination, dry mouth, excessive thirst, rapid heartbeat, or dizziness. You may also need to switch to a bland diet to reduce stomach or intestinal irritation. Common side effects of this medication include nausea, vomiting, lightheadedness, dizziness, drowsiness, or constipation. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience any unusual or severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other opioids (such as codeine or morphine), or papaverine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Avoid alcoholic beverages, as this product contains alcohol. Use caution if you have diabetes, liver disease, or any condition requiring you to limit or avoid alcohol in your diet. Women of childbearing age should discuss the risks and benefits of this medication with their doctor before use. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your doctor. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed, as it may slightly increase the risk of birth defects if used during the first two months of pregnancy. Prolonged use or high doses near the expected delivery date may harm the unborn baby. To reduce risks, use the smallest effective dose for the shortest time possible. This medication passes into breast milk and may affect a nursing infant. Notify your doctor immediately if your baby shows unusual sleepiness, feeding difficulties, or breathing problems.
